User Story: As a developer, I need a verified relational database design so that all modules store data consistently.
Acceptance Criteria: 16 tables created from schema.sql with primary keys, foreign keys, CHECK and UNIQUE constraints. | ER diagram, sample data and verification report delivered; verify_schema.py reports 0 failed checks.

User Story: As a staff member, I want to log in securely so that only authorised people use HMS.
Acceptance Criteria: Empty form or wrong password is rejected with a clear message. | Correct login (admin@hms.test) opens the dashboard; password is stored only as a salted hash.

User Story: As a receptionist, I want to register, edit, search and delete patients so that patient data is always current.
Acceptance Criteria: Required fields (first name, phone, date of birth) and formats are validated before saving. | A saved patient appears as a new row in the patients table. | Deleting a patient who has appointments is refused by the database (foreign key RESTRICT).

User Story: As an administrator, I want to manage doctors and departments so that appointments can be assigned.
Acceptance Criteria: A doctor can be added/edited with department, fee and working days. | Doctor list can be searched and filtered by department.

User Story: As a receptionist, I want to book appointments with department, doctor, date and slot, and never double-book a doctor.
Acceptance Criteria: Doctor list depends on the chosen department; time slots are offered for the chosen date. | Selecting an already booked slot shows a warning in the form. | Even if the form is bypassed, the database refuses two active appointments for the same doctor, date and time.

User Story: As a doctor, I want to record visits with diagnosis and vitals so that medical history is complete.
Acceptance Criteria: Optional vitals are range-checked (e.g. temperature, pulse); systolic must be higher than diastolic. | Blood pressure is stored as two numbers; a patient's visit history lists all records.

User Story: As a billing clerk, I want to create invoices with live totals, discount and tax so that patients are billed correctly.
Acceptance Criteria: Invoice supports several item rows; subtotal, discount, tax and total update live. | Items are stored as separate rows; total is computed by a view, never stored. | Payment status (unpaid / partial / paid) is saved and shown.

User Story: As a pharmacist, I want to manage medicine stock with expiry and low-stock warnings so that nothing runs out or expires.
Acceptance Criteria: Medicine can be added with batch, expiry, quantity and price. | Expired and low-stock medicines are flagged in the list and in alerts.

User Story: As a pharmacist, I want to dispense medicine and have stock reduce automatically so that stock is always accurate.
Acceptance Criteria: Dispensing writes a history row and reduces medicines.quantity. | Dispensing more than the available stock is refused by the server.

User Story: As the team, we want automatic tests so that we can prove the Increment works.
Acceptance Criteria: python tests/test_api.py passes all 86 checks; HMS_DB/verify_schema.py passes all 48 checks. | selftest.html reports 0 failed; 44 browser checks recorded in e2e_browser_results.txt.

User Story: As a doctor, I want a patient profile with a timeline of appointments, records, bills and dispensing so that I see the full picture.
Acceptance Criteria: Profile shows appointments, records, prescriptions, invoices and dispensing for one patient. | Timeline can be filtered by type.

User Story: As a receptionist, I want doctor schedules and an 'available today' filter so that I book the right doctor.
Acceptance Criteria: Working days come from doctor_schedules (one row per day). | 'Available today' filter lists only doctors working today; doctor profile page opens.

User Story: As a doctor, I want to add prescriptions to a visit so that medicines are recorded with the record.
Acceptance Criteria: Several prescription rows can be added to one medical record. | Prescriptions appear in the patient profile timeline.

User Story: As a manager, I want a dashboard with key numbers and alerts so that I see what needs attention.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard cards, alerts, today's schedule and a chart are read from the database. | Clicking a card opens the related module.

User Story: As a manager, I want reports across modules so that I can review hospital activity.
Acceptance Criteria: Reports page summarises patients, appointments, billing and pharmacy figures from the database.

User Story: As an auditor, I want every insert, update and delete logged so that changes can be traced.
Acceptance Criteria: Every insert, update and delete creates a row in audit_log with table, action and time.

User Story: As a staff member, I want notifications with read/unread state so that I do not miss low stock or unpaid bills.
Acceptance Criteria: Alerts are generated from stock, unpaid bills and follow-ups. | Marking an alert read is stored per user in notification_reads.

User Story: As a staff member, I want one global search across modules so that I can find records quickly.
Acceptance Criteria: Searching a name or code returns matches from patients, doctors, appointments, records, invoices and medicines.

User Story: As an administrator, I want role-based access (doctor, receptionist, pharmacist) so that users only see what they need.
As a patient, I want SMS/email appointment reminders so that I do not miss visits.
As a billing clerk, I want to print or export invoices as PDF so that I can give them to patients.
As the hospital, we want to migrate to PostgreSQL and host online so that several branches can use HMS.
